judgment.rationale: The answer satisfies the requested three-axis structure, keeps limitations visible, avoids personal medication advice, and includes clinician questions. Several general claims are supported by the supplied DailyMed and PubMed evidence, including pregnancy-associated decreases in lamotrigine concentrations with postpartum restoration, fetal exposure through placental transfer, generally reassuring monotherapy malformation findings, and uncertainty about rare outcomes and neurodevelopment. However, it fails the citation and PK criteria. The detailed maternal pharmacokinetic section cites two PubMed URLs that are not in the reference pool and does not preserve the retrieved study population and design from the available MONEAD abstract (prospective observational multicenter cohort of pregnant and nonpregnant women with epilepsy). It also attributes increased clearance mainly to glucuronidation and renal/physiologic changes without direct support in the supplied evidence. The clause "with the largest changes often reported in the second and third trimesters" is in tension with the supplied MONEAD evidence, which reports that clearance changes were commonly already present early, with half of the maximum change reached by approximately 12 weeks. The fetal-exposure section cites Newport et al., but that cited study is absent from the pool even though other supplied studies support placental transfer. Registry, oral-cleft, and MotherToBaby citations are likewise not verifiable from the supplied reference pool. The source-label content also says dose adjustments may be necessary, and the answer appropriately distinguishes this from individualized decisions, but it does not explicitly identify the available Clinical Considerations label as DailyMed; instead it links to an unverified FDA URL.
